candidates.name: Web_Scrape (AirDNA Surrey BC)
candidates.what_it_holds: Two committed CSVs (AirDNA_Surrey.csv, AirDNA_Surrey_2.csv) pulled via requests+BeautifulSoup against AirDNA's API for one city, Surrey, BC, Canada. Fields and date range not confirmed by fetch (page render limited); 10 commits total, author describes analysis as 'very basic'.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from a free/scraped AirDNA source) even though scope is a single small Canadian city — worth a manual pull to see actual columns (likely occupancy/ADR/revenue estimates AirDNA shows on its public city pages).

candidates.name: air_dna_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium scraper (Ruby) configured to pull general AirDNA city-level data for cities in Washington State. Single commit; no confirmed committed data output, appears to be the scraping method only.
candidates.why_useful: A working method to reproduce AirDNA's public city-summary numbers (occupancy/ADR/RevPAR) for WA cities without a paid account, addressing gap #2. Would need to be run to get data; per repo rules only catalogued, not run.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/airdna
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent third-party API surface documentation/profile of the AirDNA Enterprise API (market metrics, STR listing data, comparable-property sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates, Smart Rates pricing) via Bearer-auth REST. Documentation/OpenAPI-style profile, not a data dump; requires a paid AirDNA account/API key to actually pull.
candidates.why_useful: Useful map of exactly which AirDNA fields (occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, booking lead time, length of stay) are available programmatically, if the team ever gets legitimate API access; not itself usable without a paid key.

candidates.name: AirDNA GitHub org (incl. dna_util)
candidates.what_it_holds: AirDNA's own official GitHub org; public repos are engineering/data-science utility libraries (e.g. dna_util), not market data dumps. No committed market CSVs found.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms AirDNA does not publish its market data as open GitHub datasets; only useful as a place to recheck periodically for a public sample-data repo.

candidates.name: mashvisor/us-neighborhoods-boundaries
candidates.what_it_holds: GeoJSON/CSV shapefile converter and output for Zillow Neighborhood Boundaries covering 42 US states, published by Mashvisor's own GitHub org.
candidates.why_useful: Not rental-performance data, but a committed, ready-to-use neighborhood-boundary geodataset (42 states) useful for joining any city-level STR/ADR series to consistent neighborhood polygons -- infrastructure for gap #2/#13 style work, not itself a KPI series.

candidates.name: project_1 (MashvisorTopMarkets.ipynb)
candidates.what_it_holds: Jupyter notebook pulling 'top markets' data from the Mashvisor API (not a committed CSV in the repo itself; data is fetched live from Mashvisor's paid API at run time).
candidates.why_useful: Shows the Mashvisor API fields used for market ranking (cash-on-cash return, ADR-adjacent metrics) but requires a Mashvisor API key to reproduce -- low value without credentials.

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (Urban Politics and Governance Lab, McGill, David Wachsmuth) with functions explicitly designed to clean, compress and expand raw AirDNA data files, generate reliable location estimates for STR listings, and flag commercial operators / frequently-rented entire-home listings / 'ghost hostels'. Tooling only -- expects the user to supply their own AirDNA extract; on CRAN-style docs at rdrr.io/github/UPGo-McGill/strr.
candidates.why_useful: A vetted, published-research-grade processing pipeline for AirDNA-style listing/calendar data (used in the group's peer-reviewed Canadian STR studies); if the team or a licensed partner ever obtains any AirDNA extract, this is the standard method to turn it into occupancy/ADR/commercial-operator classifications. Also signals what an academic AirDNA-based methodology looks like for gap #2.
candidates.geography: method is city-agnostic; group's own use is Canada-wide
candidates.time_coverage: package current as of its releases; underlying studies use multi-year AirDNA panels (2016-2020ish per UPGo's published Canadian reports)
candidates.size_hint: R package, no data files bundled

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/canada-analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed R analysis code for Combs et al. 2019 ('Short-term cities: Airbnb's impact on Canadian housing markets'), the group's peer-reviewed study built on a 143-million-datapoint proprietary AirDNA-derived panel of daily Airbnb activity across Canadian cities (Montreal, Toronto, Vancouver and others) roughly 2016-2019. Repo structure shows an R/ directory, LICENSE, README; underlying raw AirDNA data itself is NOT committed (proprietary), only the analysis code.
candidates.why_useful: Full, citable, peer-reviewed replication code for a large-scale AirDNA-based STR study; documents exactly how commercial-operator share and revenue concentration were computed from AirDNA data, which is directly on-point for gap #2, even though the raw data underneath is not open.
candidates.time_coverage: ~2016-2019 (per published UPGo reports referencing this code)
candidates.size_hint: R analysis scripts, MIT license, 20 commits

candidates.name: urbanbigdatacentre/ubdc-airbnb
candidates.what_it_holds: Containerized, continuously-running Airbnb calendar/listing scraper framework from the University of Glasgow's Urban Big Data Centre, built for the peer-reviewed PLOS ONE 2024 paper 'Enhancing our understanding of short-term rental activity: A daily scrape-based approach for Airbnb listings' (exploits UK COVID-lockdown period). User defines their own areas of interest; the framework computes activity-level indicators from daily calendar scrapes (a realised-occupancy-style proxy built directly from calendars, not AirDNA). No committed market data in the repo itself -- it is infrastructure, and the underlying scrape is of airbnb.com itself.
candidates.why_useful: A peer-reviewed, published methodology for turning raw Airbnb calendar scrapes into occupancy/activity-level indicators without an AirDNA subscription -- directly relevant to gap #2 as an alternative construction method, and cross-relevant to the team's own Inside-Airbnb calendar work. NOTE: running this against airbnb.com is a scraping decision the CLAUDE.md rules reserve for a human (rule 6) -- catalogue only, do not run.
candidates.geography: UK (paper's case study); framework is geography-agnostic
candidates.time_coverage: paper covers UK first COVID-19 lockdown period (2020)

candidates.name: luminati-io/Airbnb-dataset-samples (Bright Data)
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSV airbnb-properties-information.csv with 1,001 Airbnb listing records (a promotional sample of Bright Data's >11M-record commercial dataset), 18+ fields including price, reviews, ratings, guest capacity, available_dates, lat/long, host info and amenities. Geographic scope described only as 'popular destinations', not itemised. 5 commits; no explicit license (Bright Data promotional sample).
candidates.why_useful: A committed, free sample of a large third-party Airbnb listing/price/availability dataset (not AirDNA, but a comparable commercial 'sample export' in scope for this theme); available_dates field could feed a lightweight occupancy proxy for whatever cities appear in the 1,001 rows. Small and not point-in-time, so low standalone value, but worth noting as a template for what Bright Data (and similar vendors) will give away.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: smaller and less rigorous than existing Inside Airbnb 13-city panel; only useful if it covers markets IA does not

candidates.name: AirROI Data Portal
candidates.what_it_holds: Non-GitHub commercial data portal claiming 20M+ listings across 190+ countries and 100,000+ markets, daily-refreshed, with free occupancy rates, revenue estimates, pricing trends, and downloadable CSV/JSON/Parquet exports; also referenced as having a GitHub-hosted Claude-Code tool that generates instant STR income reports from an Airbnb listing URL. No confirmation of a committed open dataset on GitHub -- the free tier appears to be a hosted web tool, not a repo.
candidates.why_useful: If AirROI's 'free' occupancy/revenue-estimate tier is genuinely queryable without payment, it would be a broader (and more current) analogue to AirDNA for gap #2 (190+ countries vs AirDNA's already-covered patch); flagging for a human to check the actual free-tier terms and whether a GitHub client exists, since scraping it is out of scope for this pass.

candidates.name: Rabbu-Airbnb GitHub org
candidates.what_it_holds: Rabbu's own GitHub org page surfaced in search but content not verifiable by fetch in this pass (search budget exhausted before verification); Rabbu's public web tool (rabbu.com/airbnb-data) offers free market-level occupancy, ADR, RevPAR/RevPAN and seasonal-trend stats refreshed weekly across US markets, sourced from public Airbnb/Vrbo listing data.
candidates.why_useful: Same class of free market-level STR stats as AirDNA/AirROI for gap #2; the org's actual repo contents are UNVERIFIED this pass -- flagged for a follow-up scout or manual check of https://github.com/Rabbu-Airbnb repos before relying on it.

notes: This theme is structurally thin: AirDNA, Mashvisor, AllTheRooms, Key Data, Rabbu and Awning are all paid SaaS vendors whose GitHub presence is limited to (a) their own engineering/utility repos with no market data, (b) small hobbyist scraper/wrapper repos that either don't commit their pulled data or commit a trivial single-city sample, and (c) academic groups (UPGo-McGill, Urban Big Data Centre/Glasgow) that build methodology on top of AirDNA or raw calendar scrapes without redistributing the underlying proprietary data. 'Transparent' (OTA Insight/Smart Rental) and 'Key Data' (keydatadashboard.com, keydata.co) returned no GitHub presence at all -- pure commercial dashboards, not developer-oriented, so nothing to catalogue. AllTheRooms' GitHub org is exclusively internal web-dev tooling (Node.js HTTP helpers, a slider widget), unrelated to their STR data product. The single most promising lead for gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs from a free source) is methodological, not a dataset: the UBDC daily-calendar-scrape framework (peer-reviewed, PLOS ONE 2024) and UPGo-McGill's strr package, both of which show how to derive occupancy-style indicators from calendar data without a paid AirDNA subscription -- exactly the construction the team's own Inside Airbnb calendar work already attempts, so these are best read as methodology cross-checks rather than new data. AirROI's claimed free global tier is worth a human look (not scraped here) since its stated coverage (190+ countries, daily) would exceed anything else catalogued for this gap if genuinely free and stable. Web search budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) partway through verification, before I could check Awning.com, a direct Kaggle search for 'airdna', or fully verify the Rabbu-Airbnb org's actual repo contents -- a follow-up scout should pick up those three threads specifically. No candidate here rises above medium potential; none directly fills a numbered gap with a large committed dataset -- this theme's commercial vendors simply do not open-source their market data.
